messages:
sasha: heads-up: during our long-context perf sweep on dedicated-gpu-pool-7 I'm seeing steady KV cache RSS growth over hours. hosted-api is flat under same workload; private-onprem shows bursty fragmentation after GC cycles. not an instant leak, more a slow accumulation across sessions.

jamal: which model and sequence lengths? can you repro in the perf harness?

sasha: repro is easy with the kv_load harness. model=redwood-gpt-xl, seq=10000-14000, concurrent sessions ~30, repeated prefixes overlapping ~40%. run: 
```
python infra/perf/kv_load.py --model redwood-gpt-xl --max-tokens 13000 --sessions 30 --repeats 25 --pool dedicated-gpu-7
```
After ~4h dedicated RSS climbed ~3.4GB. hosted pool (api-prod) stayed ±200MB. private-onprem1 had periodic fragmentation spikes post-GC.

mel: share the runtime kv metrics snapshot and allocator hints (jemalloc stats / mallctl). kernel versions differ? Those env diffs often explain divergent behavior.

sasha: quick snapshot mid-run: 
```
kv_cache.entries_active: 6_200_512
kv_cache.allocated_bytes: 3.6GB
kv_cache.rss_bytes: 6.1GB
kv_cache.evictions_total: 68
kv_cache.reuse_hit_ratio: 0.135
jemalloc.decay_ms: dedicated=automatic, hosted=10000
kernel: dedicated=5.15.0-88, hosted=6.2.0-26, private=vary(5.10->5.15)
```
noticed reuse_hit_ratio slowly trending down as run proceeds.

elaine: 0.135 is pretty low for these workloads. suggests eviction churn caused by our prefix cache sizing or batching pattern causing low temporal locality. Also dedicated using older kernel + default jemalloc could cause increased fragmentation.

anika: can you give pmap / proc/slabinfo snippet? curious about object size distribution and whether frames are staying resident or being swapped out.

sasha: pasted trimmed outputs: 
```
$ pmap -x $PID | tail -n4
000055c800000-000055cc0000    4194304    4133120 Rss
00007f4b0000-00007f500000    5242880    5184000 Rss

/proc/slabinfo excerpt:
kv_cache_slab: objs 6200512 active_objs 6150000 objsize 640
```
objsize ~640 aligns with some extra metadata per entry. dedicated shows many small live slabs.

mel: two immediate experiments: 1) reduce prefix retention (max_prefix_cache_entries) to force earlier eviction of low-reuse prefixes; 2) bump jemalloc decay window on dedicated to match hosted. If we can't change jemalloc globally, try per-process mallctl in the runtime before heavy load.

jamal: also check kernel page reclaim settings (swappiness, zone_reclaim) and hugepage configuration. private cluster has a locked-down sysctl policy so we may not toggle hugepages there without infra approval.

mel: propose a targeted canary on dedicated-gpu-7: 
```
runtime.kv.max_prefix_cache_entries=900000
runtime.kv.reuse_threshold=0.55
mallctl: decay_ms=10000 (set at process start)
```
run same harness for 4h and collect pmap, jemalloc stats, slabinfo every 20m.

sasha: will kick that off. note: I found a behavioral change around commit f3b9d1c where kernel-selection fallback altered warmup kernels -> could shift allocation patterns on dedicated pools. pinning that commit vs previous helps isolate.

anika: good call. also capture batching histograms; our continuous-batching heuristic might be evicting prefixes earlier if batch windows change under the new kernel path. low reuse could be batching-driven.

mel: add a lightweight probe to emit runtime.batching.window_ms and runtime.batching.avg_batch_size to metrics so we can correlate batch shape with reuse_rate.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: apply runtime.kv canary -> pool=dedicated-gpu-7 @ 2026-03-19T09:00Z (rolling, 10% of nodes)

sasha: thanks. I'll attach full jemalloc mallctl dumps and perf harness logs to the ticket. If the canary looks good we can try rolling the jemalloc decay change to hosted to test parity, but hosted kernel/jemalloc already tuned so behavior may still differ.

jamal: if fragmentation persists after canary, plan B: enable periodic compacting sweep for kv slabs (stop-gap) and schedule deeper perf mem + numa mapping capture. we should also evaluate enabling 64k hugepages on dedicated long-term if it stabilizes residency.

elaine: note on compliance: private/onprem clusters require audit board signoff before changing hugepage or CAP_SYS_ADMIN ops. so mitigation for private will likely be runtime-level (tighter prefix caps / adaptive eviction).

sasha: running canary now. will post results + pmap/slab dumps in ~3.5h. opening TICKET-ENGRT-4821 with reproducer, commit pins, and diagnostics. assigning to eng-runtime + infra for follow-up. :thumbsup:
